items.followUp: State two differences between distance and displacement.

rubric.why: Mass is the amount of matter in a body and is measured in kilograms.
rubric.description: Defines mass and gives its unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying mass as the amount of matter and/or giving its SI unit, kilogram.

rubric.why: Weight is the gravitational force on a body and is measured in newtons; it can vary with gravitational field strength.
rubric.description: Defines weight and distinguishes it from mass.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying weight as gravitational force and/or giving its SI unit, newton.

modelAnswer: Mass is the amount of matter in a body; its SI unit is kilogram (kg).
Weight is the gravitational force acting on a body; its SI unit is newton (N), and it changes with gravitational field strength.

items.followUp: State the principle of conservation of energy.

rubric.why: The law states that total momentum before an interaction equals total momentum after it.
rubric.description: States that total momentum remains unchanged.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the total momentum of the system is conserved.

rubric.why: Momentum is conserved when no external force acts on the system.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for specifying an isolated system or absence of external force.

modelAnswer: The total momentum of an isolated system remains constant, provided no external force acts on it.
Thus, total momentum before an interaction equals total momentum after it.

items.followUp: Explain how the resultant of two unlike parallel forces is found.

rubric.why: Like parallel forces act in the same direction.
rubric.description: Describes the directions of like parallel forces.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that like parallel forces act in the same direction.

rubric.why: Unlike parallel forces act in opposite directions.
rubric.description: Describes the directions of unlike parallel forces.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that unlike parallel forces act in opposite directions.

modelAnswer: Like parallel forces are parallel forces that act in the same direction.
Unlike parallel forces are parallel forces that act in opposite directions.

items.followUp: Define the moment of a force and state how it is calculated.

rubric.why: Torque is the turning effect of a force about an axis or pivot.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying torque as the turning effect of a force about an axis or pivot.

rubric.why: The moment arm is the perpendicular distance from the axis or pivot to the force's line of action.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving the perpendicular distance from the pivot or axis to the line of action of the force.

modelAnswer: Torque is the turning effect of a force about an axis or pivot.
The moment arm is the perpendicular distance from the axis or pivot to the line of action of the force.

items.followUp: Write the equation for gravitational potential energy and define its symbols.

rubric.why: Kinetic energy is the energy a body possesses because of its motion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking the energy possessed by a body to its motion.

rubric.why: The equation for kinetic energy is KE = ½mv².
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for writing the correct equation.

modelAnswer: Kinetic energy is the energy possessed by a body due to its motion.
Its mathematical equation is KE = ½mv², where m is mass and v is speed.

items.followUp: Define work and state its SI unit.

rubric.why: Power is the rate of doing work or transferring energy per unit time.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining power as work done or energy transferred per unit time.

rubric.why: The SI unit of power is the watt, equal to one joule per second.
rubric.description: States the SI unit of power.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating watt (W) or joule per second.

modelAnswer: Power is the rate of doing work, or transferring energy, per unit time.
Its SI unit is the watt (W), where 1 W = 1 J/s.

items.followUp: What is the elastic limit of a material?

rubric.why: An elastic body returns to its original shape or size after the deforming force is removed.
rubric.description: States the restoration of original shape or size.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the body returns to its original shape or size.

rubric.why: Elasticity describes this recovery after the deforming force is removed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for specifying that the recovery happens when the deforming force is removed.

modelAnswer: Elasticity is the property of a body by which it regains its original shape and size when the deforming force is removed.

items.followUp: Use a speed-time graph to derive the second equation of motion, s = ut + ½at².

rubric.why: The displacement is the area under the speed-time graph, a trapezium made up of a rectangle and a triangle.
rubric.description: Expresses displacement as the graph's area.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for using the trapezium area or the equivalent rectangle-plus-triangle area.

rubric.why: For constant acceleration, the change in speed is at.
rubric.description: Uses the first equation of motion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the relation between initial speed, final speed, acceleration, and time.

rubric.why: Substituting t = (v-u)/a into the displacement expression gives 2as = (u+v)(v-u).
rubric.description: Eliminates time to relate displacement and speeds.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid time-elimination step leading to 2as = v² − u².

rubric.why: Rearranging gives the third equation of motion.
rubric.description: States the derived third equation of motion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the final equation v² = u² + 2as.

modelAnswer: Let the initial speed be u, the final speed be v, the time be t, the acceleration be a, and the displacement be s.
From the speed-time graph, displacement equals the area under the graph: s = ut + ½(v − u)t.
From the first equation of motion, v = u + at, so t = (v − u)/a.
Substitute for t: s = ½(u + v)(v − u)/a.
